\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{لون} (lawn)}{لون (lawn)}]{\ar{لون} (lawn) — a colour}

\label{lesson:AR-C98-lawn}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for fifty, then the Arabic for a thousand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{لون}}
\textbf{\ar{لون}} — \emph{lawn} — \textquotedblleft{}a colour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{لون}} (\emph{lawn}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{l-w-n}, \textquotedblleft{}colour\textquotedblright{} (Lane). An old noun with its own root in Lane.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عطلة}}
\textbf{\ar{عطلة}} — \emph{ʿuṭla} — \textquotedblleft{}a holiday\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عطلة}} (\emph{ʿuṭla}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-ṭ-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be without work\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane's \emph{ʿuṭla} is the state of being without work; a holiday is time off work.
\end{cousinweb}
